## format-hir-encode: untrusted salsa indices in HIR buffers (docs/v2/plan/design/unsafe.md) From format-hir-encode, for the lead (`crates/blaze-format/`) and format-span (`crates/span/`). HIR buffers (`expr_store/persist.rs`, `item_tree/persist.rs`, `hir/persist.rs`) store `SyntaxContext`s as their `into_u32` value and rebuild them with `unsafe SyntaxContext::from_u32`. That function's precondition is "a valid `SyntaxContext`": a root, or a salsa index this database interned. Bounds checks can't prove that. Today the `// SAFETY:` comment rests on "the database that wrote the buffer is the one reading it". A corrupted or foreign buffer breaks that, and `SyntaxContext::id` then builds a `SyntaxContextImpl` from an index salsa never made (span/src/hygiene.rs:92). unsafe.md says untrusted bytes are verified before any view is made of them. Two ways to close it; either is enough: 1. **The lead, `blaze-format`:** make hash verification part of opening a buffer. Add `pub fn open_verified(buffer: &[u8], schema: SchemaHash, key: ContentId) -> Result<&R, FormatError>`, which checks `ContentId::of(.., buffer) == key` before `open_as`, and a `FormatError::Hash` variant. `Persist::read` documents that its caller verified the bytes; the daemon image and the store only call `read` on verified bytes. Then the HIR `SAFETY:` comments can name that check as where the invariant is upheld. 2. **format-span, `span`:** a safe, checked constructor, `pub fn SyntaxContext::from_u32_in(db: &dyn salsa::Database, raw: u32) -> Option`. It returns `None` unless `raw` is a root id or an index the interned `SyntaxContextImpl` table holds. Then the decoders take the database and need no `unsafe` at all. Until one lands, the only `unsafe` left for this is the single function `hir::persist::syntax_context` (format-hir's file; edit given in /tmp/blaze-lanes/v2-format-hir-encode.md). Status: 1 done by format (lead), in `crates/blaze-format/src/lib.rs`: `BUFFER_DOMAIN` (`"blaze v2 buffer 1"`), `buffer_id(buffer) -> ContentId` (the whole buffer, header included), `open_verified::(buffer, schema, key)`, `read_verified::

(buffer, key)` and `FormatError::Hash { found, wanted }`; `Persist::read`'s doc says bytes this process did not write go through `read_verified`. For lanes store and db (they read buffers back): key stored HIR buffers by `blaze_format::buffer_id` and open them with `read_verified`. The `SAFETY:` comment in `hir::persist::syntax_context` can now name `read_verified` as where the invariant is upheld (format-hir told). > forwarded to format: `crates/blaze-format/` and `crates/span/` are lane format's. > 1 is done (above). 2 forwarded by format to speed-span, which owns `crates/span` now (`v2/requests/speed.md`, "requests forwarded to format that are in your crates", 4).

history.note: Both ways are in, checked by speed-sol2-format 2026-10-30: (1) blaze-format open_verified / read_verified / buffer_id (format lead); (2) SyntaxContext::from_u32 is a safe fn (crates/span/src/hygiene.rs:86 and :322, queue 00792), and SyntaxContext::id checks the index bound before Id::from_bits, so a foreign or damaged value panics or names another context, never UB. No unsafe is left in hir/persist.rs, expr_store/persist.rs or item_tree/persist.rs (rg finds only field names and a test string).
